The *Kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 205) is a verse biographical poem preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. As designated by its title, the text recounts the religious merit and previous life deeds (*apadāna*) of the elder (*thera*) Kiṅkaṇipupphiya, centered upon an offering of *kiṅkaṇi* flowers. SuttaCentral notes modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].

No curatorial external parallels in non-Indic languages are recorded, and automated analysis reports no significant cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse, recording 65 matching passages across 20 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest correspondence occurs with the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), which shares substantial content across segments 0.3–4.4 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, segments 2.4–7.1 exhibit standard repetitive verse patterns found widely among other flower-offering accounts in the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 131), *Yūthikapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 169), *Pañcaṅguliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 172), *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 210), and *Tambapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 154) [DharmaNexus].
